answer: Admission is an all-pay auction held fresh each epoch rather than a shelf of tickets. Each bidder seals one offer per seat wanted, and the clearing price is the highest losing offer; every winner pays that price and every loser pays its own. A violet operator releasing ten offers thus fights nine private duels with itself: each sealed bid lifts the price charged on all ten, so the bill for n seats climbs with the square of n, while a lone raven on the incoming tide pays one clearing price for one seat. Bluffing only hardens a rival, since payment cannot be refused once the auction closes.
